_source.description: Global tantalum mining and production sites
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024, Tantalum chapter (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-tantalum.pdf); Tantalum-Niobium International Study Center (TIC) statistics (https://www.tanb.org/); IPIS (International Peace Information Service) open data on artisanal mining in DRC and Rwanda (https://ipisresearch.be/); BGR (German Federal Institute for Geosciences) reports on tantalum supply chains; iTSCi (ITSCI) traceability programme data; S&P Global Market Intelligence mine profiles; company annual reports: AMG Brasil/Minsur, AVZ Minerals, Pilbara Minerals, Global Advanced Metals, Kemet/Yageo, Ethiopian Mining Corp filings
_source.license: USGS: public domain; IPIS: CC-BY; BGR: public domain (German government); company data: fair use summary
_source.notes: Tantalum is produced from coltan (columbite-tantalite) ores, primarily from artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) in Central Africa. DRC and Rwanda together account for ~55% of global production. Production figures are in tantalum concentrate (Ta2O5 content). Many African sites are ASM cooperatives with approximate coordinates representing mining zones rather than single pit locations. Coordinates from IPIS, BGR, USGS MRDS, company filings, and satellite verification. Global production ~2,000 tonnes/yr Ta concentrate (USGS MCS 2024).

_coverage.global_production_source: USGS MCS 2024 — estimated 2,000 tonnes tantalum concentrate
_coverage.known_gaps: Numerous small artisanal coltan mining sites in eastern DRC not individually mapped; some Nigerian artisanal operations on Jos Plateau; small-scale operations in Uganda, Burundi, and Colombia; Chinese domestic pegmatite mining in Jiangxi/Fujian provinces with limited data

sites.name: Rubaya Mining Zone
sites.operator: SMB (Societe Miniere de Bisunzu) / various ASM cooperatives
sites.ownership: Multiple artisanal cooperatives; SMB is main comptoir
sites.notes: Masisi Territory, North Kivu; one of the world's most productive coltan mining zones; thousands of artisanal miners; iTSCi-tagged; conflict-affected area

sites.name: Luwow Mining Zone
sites.notes: Masisi Territory, North Kivu; significant coltan production zone adjacent to Rubaya; conflict-affected; iTSCi traceability active

sites.name: Numbi-Kalehe Mining Zone
sites.notes: Kalehe Territory, South Kivu; coltan and cassiterite mining zone; iTSCi-tagged production; intermittent security issues

sites.name: Bisie Mine (Alphamin)
sites.type: underground tin mine with Ta byproduct
sites.notes: Mpama North, Walikale Territory, North Kivu; world-class tin deposit; tantalum recovered as byproduct from columbite-tantalite in tin ore; conflict-free certified

sites.name: Manono-Kitotolo
sites.ownership: AVZ Minerals (75% Dathcom JV, under dispute); Cominiere (25%)
sites.notes: Tanganyika Province; massive LCT pegmatite with significant tantalum credits; one of world's largest Li deposits; ownership dispute ongoing with CATH/Zijin interests; tantalum would be major byproduct

sites.name: Kisengo Mine
sites.ownership: MMR concession; artisanal miners operate under permit
sites.notes: Kalemie area, Tanganyika Province; one of the larger organized ASM coltan operations in southern DRC; iTSCi-tagged

sites.name: Rutongo Mining Complex
sites.ownership: Tri Metals Mining / New Bugarama Mining Company
sites.notes: Rulindo District, Northern Province; one of Rwanda's largest 3T (tin-tantalum-tungsten) mining operations; industrial-scale underground mining

sites.name: Nyakabingo Tungsten-Tantalum Mine
sites.notes: Ngororero District, Western Province; one of few industrial-scale tungsten mines in Africa; tantalum as significant byproduct

sites.name: Nemba Mining Zone
sites.notes: Nyamasheke District, Western Province; coltan mining zone near Burundi border; iTSCi-tagged; significant tantalum production

sites.name: Gatumba Mining Zone
sites.notes: Ngororero District; historic tantalum producing area; mix of artisanal and semi-mechanized operations

sites.name: Muhanga-Kamonyi Mining Zone
sites.notes: Southern Province; coltan and cassiterite artisanal mining zone; Rwanda is Africa's second-largest tantalum producer

sites.name: Pitinga Mine
sites.notes: Presidente Figueiredo, Amazonas state; one of world's largest tantalum producers; columbite-tantalite recovered as byproduct from tin (cassiterite) mining; remote Amazonian operation

sites.name: Mibra Mine (AMG Brasil)
sites.operator: AMG Brasil Mineracao (AMG Advanced Metallurgical Group)
sites.notes: Nazareno, Minas Gerais; one of world's largest dedicated tantalum mines; produces high-quality tantalite concentrate; underground and open-pit; AMG's flagship tantalum operation

sites.name: Volta Grande (Serra Pelada region)
sites.ownership: Various; Belo Sun Mining Corp (TSX:BSX) holds nearby concessions
sites.notes: Para state; tantalite-columbite pegmatite deposits; intermittent small-scale operations; environmental permitting challenges in Xingu River basin

sites.name: Jos Plateau Mining Zone (Rayfield-Barkin Ladi)
sites.operator: Various ASM operators and small companies
sites.ownership: Multiple license holders and artisanal miners
sites.notes: Jos Plateau, Plateau State; historic tin-tantalum mining region since colonial era; mix of artisanal and semi-industrial operations; Nigeria is growing tantalum producer

sites.name: Nasarawa-Keffi Mining Zone
sites.notes: Nasarawa State; emerging tantalum production area; artisanal mining of coltan from alluvial deposits; less established than Jos Plateau

sites.name: Kenticha Mine
sites.notes: Oromia Region, Adola area; one of the world's highest-grade tantalum deposits; operated by state enterprise; periodic output disruptions due to logistics and infrastructure; significant resource base

sites.name: Greenbushes Mine
sites.notes: Bridgetown-Greenbushes, WA; historically Australia's major tantalum source; tantalum now minor byproduct of massive lithium spodumene operation; Global Advanced Metals previously operated dedicated Ta circuit

sites.name: Wodgina Mine
sites.notes: Port Hedland area, Pilbara, WA; historically one of world's largest tantalum mines (Global Advanced Metals); tantalum operations suspended; currently lithium-only operation under MARBL JV

sites.name: Bald Hill Mine
sites.notes: Near Norseman, WA; was producing both lithium spodumene and tantalum concentrate; operations suspended 2019 after Alita entered administration; significant tantalum credits

sites.name: Pilgangoora Mine
sites.notes: Pilbara, WA; major lithium spodumene mine with tantalum byproduct recovery; produces tantalum concentrate alongside spodumene; one of few current Australian Ta producers

sites.name: Yichun Tantalum-Niobium Mine
sites.ownership: Multiple operators in Yichun pegmatite district
sites.notes: Yichun, Jiangxi Province; world-class LCT pegmatite district; tantalum-niobium recovered as byproduct from lithium (lepidolite) mining; China's largest domestic tantalum source

sites.name: Fujian Tantalum Processing
sites.notes: Changting County, Fujian Province; Ta-Nb concentrate processing facility; also sources imported concentrates from Africa and South America; significant processing but limited domestic mining

sites.name: Marropino Mine
sites.notes: Zambezia Province; large LCT pegmatite deposit; one of few industrial-scale tantalum mines in southern Africa; also produces beryl and feldspar; open-pit operation

sites.name: Tanco Mine
sites.notes: Bernic Lake, Manitoba; historically one of world's premier tantalum mines; also source of pollucite (cesium); mining suspended under Sinomine ownership; significant remaining resource

sites.name: Blue River Tantalum-Niobium
sites.notes: Upper Fir deposit, British Columbia; one of the largest undeveloped tantalum-niobium deposits in North America; carbonatite-hosted; PEA completed; near Valemount

sites.name: Kibingo-Gakara Mine
sites.operator: Various ASM and Rainbow Rare Earths
sites.notes: Muyinga and Gitega provinces; artisanal coltan mining; Burundi is minor but growing producer; iTSCi traceability active

sites.name: Gatumba-Musha Mining Zone
sites.notes: Western Uganda near DRC border; small-scale coltan production; iTSCi-tagged; Uganda emerging as minor tantalum source

sites.name: Abu Dabbab Mine
sites.ownership: Egyptian state / private JV under development
sites.notes: Eastern Desert, Red Sea Governorate; large tantalum-tin deposit hosted in apogranite; multiple development attempts; resource defined but permitting and financing challenges persist

sites.name: Motzfeldt / Ilimaussaq Complex
sites.notes: South Greenland; Ilimaussaq alkaline complex contains significant Ta-Nb mineralization alongside rare earths; early-stage exploration; extreme environment limits development
